subject: POC connectivity workback and sequencing for MAP (API keys / org / IP allowlist / VPC peering)
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novalabs.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC connectivity workback and sequencing for MAP (API keys / org / IP allowlist / VPC peering)

Hi Alex —

Following our call this morning, I’ve sketched a short sequencing for the Mutual Action Plan so your team has a clear view on the dependencies and owners. Goal is to have an environment we can start runs against by Wed, Sep 1. High-level items: 

1) Org & API keys (owner: Alex) — create NovaLabs org in Redwood console and request API keys.
2) IP allowlist (owner: Nova infra) — provide the CIDR list; we’ll add to the Hosted MAP environment and confirm connectivity.
3) VPC peering (owner: Redwood infra / Aditya) — exchange VPC IDs & peering route table details; timeframe depends on your networking calendar.
4) Test run & smoke validation (owner: Karthik / Grace) — basic generation, latency sanity, and KV caching behavior.

I attached a one-tab MAP workbook (novalabs_map_v1.xlsx) with suggested dates and who does what. Please confirm owners and any blackout dates from your infra team.

If that looks good, I’ll schedule the first checkpoint (engineering sync) for Mon, Aug 24, 11:00am PT.

Thanks —
Chloe
Chloe Martin | Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: novalabs_map_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novalabs.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@novalabs.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC connectivity workback and sequencing for MAP (API keys / org / IP allowlist / VPC peering)

Thanks Chloe — this is helpful. I’ve confirmed internally that:

- We can spin up the NovaLabs org and request API keys by EOD Aug 24. I’ll send keys to your engineering alias (infra@redwood.ai) over a one-time secure channel.
- Our network window is tight the week of Aug 24–28. We can do the IP allowlist today if you provide the outbound IPs; VPC peering will likely need a short change window (we prefer Aug 28 evening or Aug 31 morning).

Question: can Redwood provide the list of egress IPs for the hosted MAP environment and the required ports? I’ve asked Maya (network lead) to share our VPC and account details once we have the IPs.

I reviewed the MAP workbook and updated a couple of dates — see my notes in the sheet. If the peering slip to Aug 31 it will still let us run initial API checks with API keys + allowlist.

Alex
Senior Platform Engineer, NovaLabs

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@novalabs.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC connectivity workback and sequencing for MAP (API keys / org / IP allowlist / VPC peering)

Chloe / Karthik —

I’ll own the VPC peering. For NovaLabs we’ll need the following before I start the peering request: 
- Your VPC ID and account/project number
- The external ASN (if using private ASN) and intended route tables to advertise
- Security contact and an outage window preference (Alex indicated Aug 28 evening or Aug 31 morning)

From our side, shared egress IPs for the hosted MAP environment: 34.213.120.45/32, 34.213.120.46/32. Required ports: outbound TCP 443 and 9443 for metrics (9443 optional).

I’ll prepare a peering diagram and attach it to the MAP drive (vpc_peering_diagram_v2.png). If Aug 28 works for you I’ll submit the peering and request an approval window with networking.

—Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: vpc_peering_diagram_v2.png (image/png)]

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@novalabs.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@novalabs.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC connectivity workback and sequencing for MAP (API keys / org / IP allowlist / VPC peering)

Chloe / team —

We’ve added the Redwood egress IPs to our allowlist and attached the CSV for your reference (ip-allowlist.csv). VPC details below: 
- VPC ID: vpc-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h
- Account: 987654321
- Preferred peering window: Aug 31, 08:00–10:00 PT (we can confirm a narrower 30-min slot as needed)

We’ll also stand up a small test instance in the VPC to validate reachability after peering. Please confirm who will kick the peering request on your side so I can monitor the logs during the window.

Maya
Network Engineer, NovaLabs

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-25T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC connectivity workback and sequencing for MAP (API keys / org / IP allowlist / VPC peering)

Perfect — thanks for the fast turnaround, everyone. Quick summary and next steps (action owners & dates):

- Alex (Nova): Create org and share API keys securely by EOD Aug 24 — PENDING (Alex to send).
- Nova infra (Maya): Confirmed allowlist and provided ip-allowlist.csv — DONE.
- Aditya (Redwood): Submit VPC peering request and coordinate Aug 31 08:00 PT window — OWNER -> In progress.
- Karthik / Grace (Redwood Eng): Run smoke tests immediately after peering and validate token usage, latency SLOs, and KV cache behavior — target Sep 1.
- Procurement (Nova): Please advise on PO / contract timeline; we have a DocuSign ready (link below).

I’ve uploaded the updated MAP workbook and the peering diagram to our shared drive. Once Alex sends the API keys we’ll run the initial token exchange and basic generate tests. If everything passes, we’ll mark the MAP milestone as "POC env ready" and proceed to workload runs.
